questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what is the correct trigger for the new Change Request notification?
options: There is no trigger; the notification sends on a fixed schedule
A named event fired by a script, since no field condition could express this
A record condition trigger: Change Request's State field changes to Scheduled
An Inbound Email Action watching for replies
questions.explain: A direct field transition the platform can watch for natively is exactly the record condition trigger from Lesson 16 — no event scripting is needed here.

questions.q: Why does the lab call out identifying the recipient as a separate decision from the trigger?
options: Because recipients are optional and can be skipped
Because the CAB group cannot be set as a notification recipient
Because the trigger and recipient are actually configured on different tables entirely
Because picking a technically-available field that isn't actually who should be notified is the common mistake Lesson 16 warned about
questions.explain: Trigger and recipient are independent settings on the notification record; treating them as one decision risks notifying the wrong audience even with a correct trigger.

questions.q: Why does the lab attach the existing Change Notification template instead of writing a new email body?
options: Writing a new body is technically impossible on this table
Reusing the shared template keeps wording consistent with other change-related emails, and any future wording fix applies automatically everywhere it's referenced
Templates cannot contain placeholders for Change Request fields
A new notification is required to always have its own unique template
questions.explain: This is the reuse benefit from Lesson 17 — one template maintained in one place, referenced by multiple notifications.

questions.q: What does a CAB member's reply need to carry for an Inbound Email Action to match it back to the correct Change Request?
options: The CAB member's job title in the email signature
The watermark that was embedded in the original outbound notification, echoed back in the reply's quoted text
A manually typed record number in the subject line
Nothing; ServiceNow matches replies randomly to any open Change Request
questions.explain: The watermark, not a parsed subject line, is the real mechanism inbound processing uses to match a reply to its originating record, as covered in Lesson 18.

questions.q: If the notification is built correctly but no Inbound Email Action exists for the Change Request table, what is the actual outcome?
options: Replies are instead converted into brand-new Incident records
Nothing works at all — the CAB never receives the scheduled-change email
The outbound notification to the CAB works correctly, but a reply never becomes a comment on the Change Request
The notification automatically creates its own Inbound Email Action
questions.explain: The outbound half (trigger, recipient, template) and the inbound half (watermark match, Record Action) are independent pieces — a correct notification says nothing about whether the reply path exists.
